summary: Soldier Camp lookout station on the Coronado NF in the Catalina Mountains, in use by June 1921; listed as gone; no build or removal dates found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone, type unknown, by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source read gives a removal date or describes what remains

events.note: Soldier Camp was in use as a lookout station by June 1921; a fire report was received there
Small forest fire in the Canada del Oro district, Catalina Mountains; reported at the lookout station and under control by Thursday afternoon

evidence.supports: Soldier Camp lookout station in use in June 1921
evidence.quote: The fire was reported to Ranger B.G. Mettler at the Soldier Camp lookout station about 11:30 o'clock Wednesday night.

evidence.supports: fire in the Catalina Mountains, Canada del Oro district, burning since Wednesday night
evidence.quote: A small forest fire in the Catalina Mountains, in the Canada del Oro district, has been burning since Wednesday night.

evidence.supports: fire under control by Thursday afternoon
evidence.quote: Forest Ranger Smith went to the scene of the blaze with two men and reported Thursday afternoon that he and his men were holding the fire well under control.

evidence.supports: Soldier Camp is a populated place in Pima County today
evidence.quote: Soldier Camp is a populated place situated in Pima County, Arizona, United States.
It is located along the Catalina Highway in the Coronado National Forest.

evidence.supports: Soldier Trail runs from the Catalina Highway to an abandoned prison camp
evidence.quote: This trail follows the route of an old road and power line from the Catalina Highway to the site of a now-abandoned prison camp.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Soldier Camp as gone, type unknown
the newspaper report is dated June 12, 1921

corrections.why: Coronado is the name of the national forest, not a county. Wikipedia places Soldier Camp in Pima County, Arizona.

sources.title: Soldier Trail #706
sources.publisher: Coronado National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Only one primary-type item was found: a June 1921 newspaper report (Tombstone Weekly Epitaph, reprinted by Forest Lookouts). No build date, tower type, staffing history or removal date was found. The Wikipedia article and the Forest Service trail page describe the place and an abandoned prison camp, but neither says the camp is the lookout site; do not connect them without a source. The brief's county 'Coronado' is a forest name and is corrected to Pima. Access is not recorded.
